---
title: Set up deploys
guide-section: Get started
---

Deploys run on a computer on your home network (a self-hosted runner). GitHub cannot reach Home Assistant directly.

## Add a runner

1. Config repo: **Settings > Actions > Runners > New self-hosted runner**.
2. Pick the computer's OS. Run the commands GitHub shows, on that computer.
3. Install the runner as a service so it starts on boot. See GitHub's runner docs for your OS.
4. Check the runner shows **Idle**.

Runner computer needs:

- `git`, `ssh`, `rsync`.
- Passwordless SSH to Home Assistant. See [Install the add-ons](add-ons.qmd).

## Set variables

1. **Settings > Environments > New environment**. Name: `haos`.
2. Under **Environment variables**, add:

| Variable | Required | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `HA_SSH` | Yes | `root@homeassistant.local`, or `root@<IP address>` |
| `PACKAGE_REPO` | Yes, unless your account has its own copy of ha-automations | `joshwlivingston/ha-automations` |
| `HA_SSH_PORT` | No | The add-on's SSH port, if not `22` |
| `RUNNER_LABELS` | No | Runner labels as a JSON list, if not `["self-hosted"]` |

## When it deploys

| When | Deploys |
|---|---|
| Push to `main` | Your `apps.yaml`, with the latest release |
| New release | The new release, found by a scheduled check |
| By hand | **Actions > Deploy > Run workflow**. Optional: a version, and **force**. |

- Scheduled check: every 15 minutes by day, hourly overnight.
- Schedule times: UTC, set for US Mountain time. Change the `cron` lines in `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`.
- If nothing changed, the run stops.
- Each deploy restarts AppDaemon.
